questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Emergence of Macroeconomics' refers to.
questions.a: Macroeconomics as a separate branch emerged out of the Great Depression that began in 1929; microeconomic reasoning could not explain the collapse of output and employment, and John Maynard Keynes' General Theory (1936) built the analysis of economy-wide aggregates.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Emergence of Macroeconomics'.
questions.a: The Depression was the empirical puzzle that forced economists to study inflation, unemployment and national output as aggregates.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Emergence of Macroeconomics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Emergence of Macroeconomics (source: leec101.txt Great Depression narrative and Keynes references)

Explain in your own words what 'Unemployment During the Great Depression' refers to.
questions.a: In the USA, from 1929 to 1933, the unemployment rate rose from 3 per cent to 25 per cent as workers were thrown out of jobs, illustrating how an economy-wide collapse differs from a market-level disequilibrium.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unemployment During the Great Depression'.
questions.a: The rise in the unemployment rate is the difference between the peak rate in 1933 and the trough rate in 1929.

Explain in your own words what 'Stocks, Flows and Capital' refers to.
questions.a: Macroeconomics distinguishes stocks (quantities measured at a point of time, like the capital stock or wealth) from flows (quantities measured over a period, like income or investment); capital is a produced means of production that adds to the stock.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stocks, Flows and Capital'.
questions.a: Classifying a variable as stock or flow decides which accounting identity it can enter, and mixing them produces measurement errors.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Stocks, Flows and Capital' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Concepts of Macroeconomics (source: leec101.txt stock-flow discussion and capital definition)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Circular Flow of Income' refers to.
questions.a: In the simplest two-sector economy, households supply factors of production to firms and receive factor incomes; firms sell goods and services back to households, so the income of one sector is the expenditure of the other and the circular flow closes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Circular Flow of Income'.
questions.a: The circular flow identity - what is spent by firms is the income of households and what households spend is the revenue of firms - underlies all national income accounting.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Circular Flow of Income' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A Simple Economy (source: leec101.txt two-sector circular flow description and economic units)
